info: Definite articles (the, a): Russian has no articles. There is no equivalent of "the." Definiteness is usually communicated through context, word order, or emphasis.

Russian plurals are fairly systematic but depend on gender and spelling.

Common patterns:

книга → книги (book → books)
стол → столы (table → tables)
окно → окна (window → windows)

Russian also changes noun endings according to grammatical case, so plural forms can become quite complex. The basic plural is usually manageable, but the full system takes time to learn.

In Russian, pronouns are used to replace nouns for efficiency, similar to English. However, Russian pronouns vary more based on grammatical case, indicating the role in a sentence. Unlike English, where pronouns don't change much in different cases, Russian pronouns exhibit more extensive case-dependent variations. Additionally, Russian has a more formal pronoun for addressing strangers or showing respect, unlike the general "you" in English.
